cards.meaning: Arabic grammar — the science of what to do with words in a sentence
Arabic morphology — the science that gives us the words themselves
Arabic rhetoric — the subtleties of the most appropriate construction for conveying an exact meaning

cards.front: Which three sciences of the Arabic language are studied in seminary?
cards.back: نَحْو، صَرْف، بَلَاغَة

cards.front: What is the division of labour between صَرْف and نَحْو?
cards.back: صَرْف gives us the words; نَحْو tells us what to do with them

cards.front: What do نَحْو and صَرْف together produce?
cards.back: Correct Arabic

cards.front: What does بَلَاغَة add beyond correct Arabic?
cards.back: The subtleties of the most appropriate construction, and the other choices that convey an exact meaning

cards.text: The definition of نَحْو: a science which teaches (a) {{c1::how to join an اِسْم، فِعْل، or حَرْف to make a correct sentence}}, and (b) {{c2::the condition of the last letter of a word}}

cards.meaning: the condition of the last letter of a word

cards.front: What is the subject matter of نَحْو?
cards.back: The كَلِمَة / مُفْرَد (the word) and the كَلَام / جُمْلَة (the sentence)

cards.front: Why does it matter to know whether a term is being used in نَحْو or in صَرْف?
cards.back: Some terms overlap between the two sciences; knowing which science is meant fixes which sense is intended

cards.front: What is the immediate objective of studying نَحْو, صَرْف, and بَلَاغَة?
cards.back: To speak, listen, read, and write in Arabic

cards.front: What is the mid-term objective of studying نَحْو, صَرْف, and بَلَاغَة?
cards.back: To use those skills to understand the Qurʾān, ḥadīth, and Islamic texts in order to act upon them

cards.front: What is the ultimate objective of studying نَحْو, صَرْف, and بَلَاغَة?
cards.back: To gain the pleasure of Allah Most High

cards.front: Beyond language skill, what does reading the classical texts give the student?
cards.back: Connection to the tradition and history of Islamic scholarship, and nearness to Allah

cards.meaning: any sound produced by a human
an utterance to which a meaning has been assigned
an utterance to which no meaning has been assigned

cards.front: On what basis is لَفْظ divided into مَوْضُوع and مُهْمَل?
cards.back: Whether a meaning has been assigned to it — وَضْع

cards.front: What does وَضَعَ mean in Arabic studies?
cards.back: To enter something into the dictionary — i.e. to assign it a meaning in the language

cards.text: اللَّفْظ is either {{c1::مَوْضُوع::assigned a meaning}} or {{c2::مُهْمَل::left without meaning}}; and المَوْضُوع is either {{c3::مُفْرَد::one word}} or {{c4::مُرَكَّب::two or more words}}

cards.front: What is a مُفْرَد?
cards.back: A single word

cards.front: What is the other name for مُفْرَد?
cards.back: كَلِمَة

cards.text: The technical definition of كَلِمَة: {{c1::لَفْظٌ}} {{c2::مَوْضُوعٌ}} {{c3::مُفْرَدٌ}}
The كَلِمَة has three types: {{c1::اِسْم}}, {{c2::فِعْل}}, and {{c3::حَرْف}}
Classical definition of اِسْم: a كَلِمَة {{c1::whose meaning can be understood by itself}} and {{c2::which has no tense}}

cards.front: What is the modern definition of اِسْم?
cards.back: A person, place, or thing; a noun

cards.front: Which definition of اِسْم do we use, and why?
cards.back: The classical one, because we are learning classical Arabic

cards.front: What does the classical اِسْم include that “noun” does not?
cards.back: Adjectives, pronouns, adverbs, and some prepositions

cards.front: What proportion of Arabic words are اِسْم?
cards.back: The majority

cards.front: If a word is not clearly a فِعْل or a حَرْف, what is it most likely to be?
cards.back: An اِسْم

cards.front: What can an اِسْم never carry at the same time?
cards.back: Both تَنْوِين and أَلِف لَام

cards.front: When a word ends in فَتْحَتَان, what should follow it?
cards.back: An أَلِف

cards.front: What is the full exception to the “أَلِف after فَتْحَتَان” rule?
cards.back: When the فَتْحَتَان sits on a تَاء مَرْبُوطَة

cards.front: What is the partial exception to the “أَلِف after فَتْحَتَان” rule?
cards.back: When the word ends in a هَمْزَة preceded by an أَلِف

cards.text: The اِسْم has three types: {{c1::جَامِد::the primary one}}, {{c2::مَصْدَر::the root one}}, and {{c3::مُشْتَقّ::the derived one}}

cards.meaning: the “primary” اِسْم — not derived from anything, and nothing is derived from it
the “root” اِسْم — an اِسْم from which many words are derived

cards.front: The مَصْدَر is the action — but with what qualification?
cards.back: Without tense

cards.meaning: the “derived” اِسْم — derived from a مَصْدَر, whose وَزْن denotes a particular meaning

cards.front: What does the وَزْن of a مُشْتَقّ do?
cards.back: It denotes a particular meaning

cards.front: What is the difference of opinion about where verbs come from?
cards.back: Whether all verbs come from the مَصْدَر, or from the هُوَ form of the مَاضِي

cards.front: Which position on the origin of verbs do we take, and why?
cards.back: The مَصْدَر — for us it is where the rest of the meanings are derived from

cards.text: Classical definition of فِعْل: a كَلِمَة {{c1::whose meaning can be understood by itself}} and {{c2::which has tense — past, present, or future}}

cards.front: What is the modern definition of فِعْل?
cards.back: It denotes an action

cards.front: What can a فِعْل never carry?
cards.back: تَنْوِين or أَلِف لَام

cards.text: An اِسْم may never carry {{c1::both تَنْوِين and أَلِف لَام at once}}; a فِعْل may never carry {{c2::either of them at all}}

cards.front: Of جَامِد / مَصْدَر / مُشْتَقّ, which describes verbs?
cards.back: مُشْتَقّ only — verbs are always derived

cards.text: The اِسْم {{c1::has no tense}}; the فِعْل {{c2::has tense}}. Both {{c3::can be understood by themselves}}
Definition of حَرْف: a كَلِمَة {{c1::whose meaning cannot be understood without being joined to a فِعْل and/or an اِسْم}}

cards.front: What follows from the حَرْف depending on other words for its meaning?
cards.back: It will always be part of a phrase

cards.text: The اِسْم and the فِعْل {{c1::can be understood by themselves}}; the حَرْف {{c2::cannot}}

cards.meaning: a compound — two or more words, which may or may not form a complete sentence

cards.front: What does رَكَّبَ mean?
cards.back: To build or assemble something

cards.text: The مُرَكَّب is either {{c1::نَاقِص::incomplete}} or {{c2::تَامّ::complete}}; the تَامّ is what is called {{c3::كَلَام}} or {{c4::جُمْلَة}}

cards.front: What is a مُرَكَّب نَاقِص?
cards.back: An incomplete compound — it does not amount to a full sentence

cards.front: What is a مُرَكَّب تَامّ?
cards.back: A complete compound — a full sentence, i.e. a كَلَام or جُمْلَة

cards.front: What distinguishes نَاقِص from تَامّ?
cards.back: Whether the compound conveys a complete meaning — whether it is a full sentence

cards.front: Into which two types does the جُمْلَة divide?
cards.back: جُمْلَة خَبَرِيَّة and جُمْلَة إِنْشَائِيَّة

cards.text: The technical definition of a sentence in Arabic: {{c1::لَفْظٌ}} {{c2::مَوْضُوعٌ}} {{c3::مُرَكَّبٌ}} {{c4::تَامٌّ}}
كَلِمَة is لَفْظٌ مَوْضُوعٌ {{c1::مُفْرَدٌ}}; كَلَام is لَفْظٌ مَوْضُوعٌ {{c2::مُرَكَّبٌ تَامٌّ}}
cards.extra: These two definitions share three of four terms — the final term is the whole difference.

cards.text: The فِعْل has three types: {{c1::المَاضِي::past}}, {{c2::المُضَارِع::present/future}}, and {{c3::الأَمْر::command}}

cards.meaning: the present and future tense
the positive command
the negative command

cards.front: How many tenses does المُضَارِع cover?
cards.back: Two — present and future

cards.front: Why is النَّهْي not usually counted as a fourth type of فِعْل?
cards.back: Some do count it separately, but technically it is derived from المُضَارِع

cards.text: The حَرْف is either {{c1::عَامِل::causative}} or {{c2::غَيْر عَامِل::non-causative}}

cards.meaning: causative — a ḥarf which influences the إِعْرَاب of the word after it
non-causative — a ḥarf which causes no change in the grammatical state of the word after it

cards.front: On what basis is the حَرْف divided into عَامِل and غَيْر عَامِل?
cards.back: Whether it influences the إِعْرَاب of the word that follows it

cards.text: The incomplete compound is {{c1::نَاقِص}}, also called {{c2::غَيْر مُفِيد}}; the complete one is {{c3::تَامّ}}, also called {{c4::مُفِيد}}
The جُمْلَة is either {{c1::خَبَرِيَّة::can be true or false}} or {{c2::إِنْشَائِيَّة::cannot}}; the خَبَرِيَّة is either {{c3::اِسْمِيَّة}} or {{c4::فِعْلِيَّة}}

cards.meaning: a sentence which has the possibility of being true or false — a statement
a sentence which has no possibility of being true or false — such as a question or a command

cards.front: On what basis is the جُمْلَة divided into خَبَرِيَّة and إِنْشَائِيَّة?
cards.back: Whether it has the possibility of being true or false

cards.front: Which two types sit under the جُمْلَة خَبَرِيَّة?
cards.back: جُمْلَة اِسْمِيَّة خَبَرِيَّة and جُمْلَة فِعْلِيَّة خَبَرِيَّة

cards.text: The جُمْلَة اِسْمِيَّة begins with {{c1::an اِسْم}}; the جُمْلَة فِعْلِيَّة begins with {{c2::a فِعْل}}

cards.meaning: the subject — the first part of a nominal sentence
the predicate — the second part of a nominal sentence
the word about which the information is being given
the word giving the information
the doer — the second part of a verbal sentence

cards.text: In a جُمْلَة اِسْمِيَّة the مُبْتَدَأ is the {{c1::مُسْنَد إِلَيْهِ}} and the خَبَر is the {{c2::مُسْنَد}}; in a جُمْلَة فِعْلِيَّة the فِعْل is the {{c3::مُسْنَد}} and the فَاعِل is the {{c4::مُسْنَد إِلَيْهِ}}
cards.extra: They swap position between the two sentence types — the roles are what stay fixed.

cards.front: مُسْنَد and مُسْنَد إِلَيْهِ change position between the two sentence types — what stays fixed?
cards.back: The مُسْنَد is always the word giving the information, and the مُسْنَد إِلَيْهِ always the word it is given about

cards.front: Can the خَبَر of a nominal sentence be a فِعْل?
cards.back: Yes — it may be either an اِسْم or a فِعْل

cards.front: How many خَبَر may a nominal sentence have?
cards.back: More than one — there can be multiple

cards.front: What is the grammatical state of both parts of a جُمْلَة اِسْمِيَّة خَبَرِيَّة?
cards.back: Both are مَرْفُوع

cards.front: Which part of a جُمْلَة فِعْلِيَّة is always مَرْفُوع?
cards.back: The فَاعِل

cards.front: How many types does the جُمْلَة إِنْشَائِيَّة have?
cards.back: Ten

cards.front: Name the ten types of جُمْلَة إِنْشَائِيَّة. (two commands, a question, two wishes, a call, an offer, an oath, a wonder, a contract)
cards.back: الأَمْر، النَّهْي، الاِسْتِفْهَام، التَّمَنِّي، التَّرَجِّي، النِّدَاء، العَرْض، القَسَم، التَّعَجُّب، العُقُود

cards.meaning: the interrogative — asking a question
desire — wanting what you do not deserve or expect
hope — wanting what you think is possible
exclamation — calling out to someone
a request or an offer
an oath
amazement
a transaction

cards.text: {{c1::التَّمَنِّي}} is wanting what you {{c2::do not deserve or expect}}; {{c3::التَّرَجِّي}} is wanting what you {{c4::think is possible}}

cards.front: What is anomalous about العُقُود being counted as إِنْشَائِيَّة?
cards.back: In reality it is خَبَرِيَّة, but Islamic law recognises it as إِنْشَائِيَّة with respect to all contracts

cards.front: الأَمْر and النَّهْي each appear in two different classifications — which?
cards.back: As types of فِعْل, and as types of جُمْلَة إِنْشَائِيَّة

cards.front: What is the mnemonic phrase for the حُرُوف القَمَرِيَّة?
cards.back: أَبْغِ حَجَّكَ وَخَفْ عَقِيمَهْ

cards.front: What does أَبْغِ حَجَّكَ وَخَفْ عَقِيمَهْ mean?
cards.back: Seek your Hajj and fear it being fruitless — its acceptance being withheld

cards.front: How many حُرُوف قَمَرِيَّة are there?
cards.back: Fourteen

cards.text: The حُرُوف القَمَرِيَّة, from أَبْغِ حَجَّكَ وَخَفْ عَقِيمَهْ: {{c1::أ ب غ ح}} {{c2::ج ك و خ}} {{c3::ف ع ق ي}} {{c4::م ه}}
cards.extra: The mnemonic is the list — each letter of the phrase is one of them.

cards.front: How are non-intellectual plurals treated grammatically?
cards.back: As singular feminine

cards.meaning: indefinite
definite

cards.text: {{c1::تَنْوِين}} can mark an ism as {{c2::نَكِرَة::indefinite}}; {{c3::أَلِف لَام}} marks it as {{c4::مَعْرِفَة::definite}}

cards.front: How many signs of an اِسْم are there?
cards.back: Twelve

cards.text: Signs of an اِسْم (1–4): it is preceded by {{c1::أَلِف لَام}}; it accepts a {{c2::جَرّ}}; it has {{c3::تَنْوِين}} on the last letter; it ends with a {{c4::تَاء مَرْبُوطَة}}
Signs of an اِسْم (5–8): it is {{c1::مُثَنَّى}}; it is {{c2::جَمْع}}; it is a {{c3::مُسْنَد إِلَيْهِ}}; it is {{c4::مُضَاف}}
Signs of an اِسْم (9–12): it is {{c1::مَوْصُوف}}; it is {{c2::مُنَادَى}}; it is {{c3::مُصَغَّر}}; it is {{c4::مَنْسُوب}}

cards.meaning: the diminutive form
a noun converted into an adjective — spelled with a سِين
the one being called

cards.front: If مُثَنَّى and جَمْع are signs of an اِسْم, why can a مُضَارِع verb still be dual?
cards.back: Because only the ضَمِير becomes dual — the فِعْل portion itself stays the same

cards.front: How many signs of a فِعْل are there?
cards.back: Nine

cards.text: Signs of a فِعْل (1–5): preceded by {{c1::قَدْ}}; by {{c2::سـ}}; by {{c3::سَوْفَ}}; by a {{c4::حَرْف جَزْم}}; by a {{c5::حَرْف نَصْب}}
Signs of a فِعْل (6–9): it has a {{c1::ضَمِير مُسْتَتِر}}; it is {{c2::أَمْر}}; it is {{c3::نَهْي}}; it has a {{c4::تَاء التَّأْنِيث}}

cards.front: What is the sign of a حَرْف?
cards.back: That it takes none of the signs of an اِسْم or a فِعْل

cards.text: A {{c1::تَاء مَرْبُوطَة}} at the end marks an {{c2::اِسْم}}; a {{c3::تَاء التَّأْنِيث}} marks a {{c4::فِعْل}}
cards.extra: Both are a tāʾ, and they point at opposite word classes.

cards.text: {{c1::مَنْسُوب}} — with a سِين — is a noun turned into an adjective; {{c2::مَنْصُوب}} — with a صَاد — is the accusative state
cards.extra: Your notes flag this one explicitly.

cards.text: The types of مُرَكَّب نَاقِص taught so far: {{c1::التَّوْصِيفِيّ::descriptive}}, {{c2::الإِضَافِيّ::possessive}}, and {{c3::الإِشَارِيّ::demonstrative}}
cards.extra: Two more are still to come.

cards.meaning: a descriptive phrase — one word describes the other
the describing word in a التَّوْصِيفِيّ phrase
the word being described in a التَّوْصِيفِيّ phrase

cards.text: In a التَّوْصِيفِيّ phrase the صِفَة and مَوْصُوف must correspond in all four of: {{c1::grammatical state}}, {{c2::gender}}, {{c3::number}}, and {{c4::type — proper or not}}

cards.front: In how many areas must the صِفَة and the مَوْصُوف correspond?
cards.back: Four

cards.meaning: a possessive phrase — the first word is attributed to the second
the first word of an إِضَافَة — the thing attributed
the second word of an إِضَافَة — the one attributed to, which in some cases owns the first

cards.front: What can a مُضَاف never carry?
cards.back: An أَلِف لَام or a تَنْوِين

cards.front: What is the grammatical state of the مُضَاف إِلَيْهِ?
cards.back: Always مَجْرُور

cards.front: Where does the صِفَة go if the مُضَاف has one?
cards.back: After the whole إِضَافَة phrase

cards.front: Why must the صِفَة of a مُضَاف be مَعْرِفَة?
cards.back: Because the مُضَاف is technically مَعْرِفَة, and the two must correspond

cards.meaning: a demonstrative phrase — one ism points to another
the ism that does the pointing in an إِشَارِيّ phrase
the ism being pointed to

cards.text: In an إِشَارِيّ phrase the مُشَار إِلَيْهِ must carry {{c1::an أَلِف لَام}}, and must match the اِسْم الإِشَارَة in {{c2::gender and number}}

cards.front: How many types of مُرَكَّب نَاقِص are there in total, and how many have been taught?
cards.back: Five in total — three so far, with two still to come

cards.front: Can a خَبَر itself be a complete sentence?
cards.back: Yes
